phone_observation.section:
Context and resources
Homelands Before Reservation Boundaries
The Tribe's history places Mouache homelands along the eastern Rocky Mountains, from the Denver area south into New Mexico. It places Caputa homelands south of the Conejos River and in the San Luis Valley near the Rio Grande's headwaters. These are histories of the two bands that make up the Southern Ute Indian Tribe, not a map of present-day ownership or jurisdiction.Context reviewed 15 Oct 2026 with AI assistance.
Allotment And Different Paths
The Tribe recounts that the 1895 Hunter Act opened the Ute Strip to allotment, homesteading and sales to non-Indians. Its history describes Mouache and Caputa families taking individual allotments, while Weenuchiu people opposed individual landholding and moved west. Its chronology dates Southern Ute allotment distribution to 1896. The accounts explain different paths among related Ute communities; they do not make today's governments interchangeable.Context reviewed 15 Oct 2026 with AI assistance.
Restoration And Future Generations
Land loss is only part of this history. The Tribe's chronology records a Restoration Act returning land to the Southern Utes in 1937. It also records a 1984 Tribal Council resolution that made education a priority through a higher-education scholarship committee and program. These are historical milestones, not statements of today's land title, program funding or eligibility.Context reviewed 15 Oct 2026 with AI assistance.
